updateConsent.title: Check for updates?
updateConsent.intro: Mynota does everything on this computer. Recording, transcription and summaries never leave it, and nothing is sent anywhere by default.
updateConsent.exception: Update checks are the one exception, and they are off until you turn them on.
updateConsent.ifOn: If you turn them on, at every launch Mynota asks GitHub whether a newer version of Mynota exists (never while you are recording). That request sends:
updateConsent.sendsIp: your IP address, to github.com (and to objects.githubusercontent.com, which it redirects to)
updateConsent.sendsNothing: nothing else — no meeting audio, no transcripts, no summaries, no usage statistics, no identifier, no account
updateConsent.noVersion: Your version number isn't sent either. Mynota downloads the same public file every user downloads and compares versions here on your computer.
updateConsent.onlyTells: Mynota will only tell you an update exists. It will never download or install one on its own.
updateConsent.macCaveat: Note: this build isn't signed with an Apple Developer ID. Replacing Mynota with a new version changes its identity as far as macOS is concerned, so macOS will drop Mynota's microphone permission and you'll have to switch it back on in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Microphone. That's why Mynota hands you a download link instead of installing updates for you.
updateConsent.footer: You can change this any time in About › Updates.
